content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge resolves D5 against C5 by assessing whether CR2 G answers particular word rows and leaves the sign's sense open, rather than by chain-vs-chain footing.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"the pressing side's own chain read together — reading 1: K-C applies because C5 is the pressing chain against D5 and the judge decides by its verse rows; reading 2: K-C does not apply because the judge text only mentions rows and an open sign-sense, not a chain read together. I chose reading 1 because the judge is adjudicating D5 vs C5 on CR2 G's answer to those rows.","why":"The judge treats the collision as underdetermined because the word-level sign sense remains open rather than weighing the chains' relative footing, so it applies the retired verse-by-verse test."}
